app.name: Suraksha
app.tagline: Check a suspicious message before you trust it

footer.disclaimer: Suraksha is a safety assistant, not a guarantee. If you are unsure, call your bank's official number — from your passbook or your branch — never a number from the message.

home.heading: Got a suspicious message?
home.subheading: Paste it here. Suraksha will tell you if it is a scam — and why.
home.placeholder: Paste the SMS, WhatsApp message or link here…
home.emptyError: Paste or type a message first.

check.noReasons: No known scam signals were found. Stay careful — a clean check is not a guarantee.
check.overrideNote: One signal here is dangerous on its own, so the verdict is raised regardless of the rest.
check.emptyState: No message to check. Go back and paste one.

ai.downloading: Downloading the AI model once — after this it works offline.

check.tacticsHeading: What this message is doing to you
check.archetypeNextLabel: What they will ask for next

verdictLine.safe: No scam signals found — but always stay alert.
verdictLine.caution: Some warning signs. Do not act in a hurry; verify first.
verdictLine.risky: Several scam signs. Treat this as a scam until you have verified it.
verdictLine.danger: This is a scam. Do not share any code, do not pay, do not install anything.

credential.secretAsk: It asks for your OTP, PIN or password. No bank, wallet or official ever asks for these — anyone who does is stealing.
credential.remoteAccess: It mentions a screen-sharing app like AnyDesk or TeamViewer. Scammers use these to watch your phone and empty your account.
credential.installApp: It tells you to install an app or switch on special permissions. This is how scammers take control of phones.

upi.collectToReceive: It says entering your UPI PIN or approving a request will bring you money. Your PIN only ever sends money OUT — receiving needs nothing.
upi.qrReceive: It asks you to scan a QR code to receive money. Receiving money never needs a QR scan.
upi.wrongTransferReturn: It claims money reached you by mistake and asks you to send it back. This is a known trap — check your own bank app, then talk to your branch.
upi.refundBait: It dangles a refund or cashback out of nowhere. Fake refunds are used to make you approve payments.
upi.unusualVpa: The UPI ID uses an uncommon provider. Check the receiver's name in your UPI app before paying anything.

url.knownPhishing: This exact link has been reported as a scam or phishing site by security services. Do not open it.
url.apkDownload: It links to an app file (APK/EXE) download. Apps from links can watch your screen and empty your account — install only from the Play Store.
url.lookalikeDomain: The website address imitates a real bank or service, but it is not the official address.
url.punycodeHomoglyph: The link uses look-alike characters to disguise a fake website address.
url.shortener: The link is shortened, hiding where it really leads. Banks and offices do not send shortened links.
url.ipAddress: The link points to a raw number address instead of a real website name. No bank does this.
url.suspiciousTld: The website ends in a cheap domain that fraudsters commonly use.
url.httpBank: A link about banking is not using a secure (https) address. Real bank sites are always secure.
url.govClaimNonGov: It talks about a government scheme, but the link is not a government (.gov.in) website.
url.excessiveSubdomains: The web address is stretched with many extra parts to look official. Genuine addresses are short.

loan.advanceFee: It asks for a fee, GST or deposit before giving the loan. Real lenders take charges from the loan amount — never pay money to get a loan.
loan.tooEasy: It promises a loan with no documents, no credit check or 'guaranteed' approval. Real loans always need checks; this is bait.
loan.rbiClaim: It claims to be 'RBI approved'. The RBI does not approve individual lenders — check the lender on the RBI website's NBFC list.

impersonation.authorityClaim: It claims to be from a bank, the police, RBI, income tax or a courier. Anyone can say this on a call — verify through an official number, not this message.
impersonation.digitalArrest: It threatens arrest, a warrant or a seized parcel to frighten you. This is the 'digital arrest' scam — the police never arrest or take payment over a call.
impersonation.senderIdMismatch: It claims to be your bank but gives a personal 10-digit mobile number. Real bank messages never ask you to call a personal number.

urgency.deadline: It creates a rush — 'act now', 'within hours', 'account blocked today'. This pressure is meant to stop you thinking. Slow down and verify.
urgency.secrecy: It tells you to keep this secret from family or bank staff. Honest institutions never ask for secrecy — this is how victims are cut off from help.

reward.lotteryPrize: It says you won a lottery, prize or lucky draw you never entered. Real prizes never need you to pay or share details to claim.
reward.jobUpfront: It offers easy earnings but asks for a registration or joining fee first. Real jobs pay you — they never ask you to pay to start.
reward.investment: It promises guaranteed profit or doubled money. No real investment is guaranteed; 'sure profit' offers are traps.

textual.excessiveCaps: The message is mostly in capital letters to shout and rush you. Genuine messages rarely do this.
textual.charSubstitution: Words like 'account' or 'OTP' are spelled with digits or symbols to slip past filters — a common scam trick.
textual.homoglyphWord: A word uses look-alike letters from another alphabet to disguise itself. This is deliberate trickery.

kyc-expiry.name: KYC expiry scam
kyc-expiry.summary: A fake bank message says your KYC has expired and the account will be blocked unless you verify through their link.
kyc-expiry.nextStep: Next they will ask for your OTP or card details, or push you to a fake login page.

upi-collect.name: UPI collect-request trap
upi-collect.summary: You are asked to approve a request or enter your UPI PIN to 'receive' money — but a PIN only ever sends money out.
upi-collect.nextStep: Next they will send a collect request and rush you to approve it or enter your PIN.

refund-reversal.name: Wrong-transfer refund scam
refund-reversal.summary: Someone claims they sent you money by mistake and begs you to return it, often after a fake credit SMS.
refund-reversal.nextStep: Next they will send a fake 'money received' message and press you to transfer it back.

digital-arrest.name: Digital arrest scam
digital-arrest.summary: Fake police or CBI officers claim you are in a criminal case and keep you on call, isolated, to extract money.
digital-arrest.nextStep: Next they will demand secrecy, a video call, and a 'verification' transfer to clear your name.

courier-parcel.name: Courier / parcel scam
courier-parcel.summary: A courier or customs 'officer' says a parcel in your name holds illegal items and you must pay to avoid arrest.
courier-parcel.nextStep: Next they will transfer you to a fake officer and demand a clearance or fine payment.

electricity-bill.name: Electricity disconnection scam
electricity-bill.summary: A message threatens to cut your power tonight over an unpaid bill and tells you to call a number or pay now.
electricity-bill.nextStep: Next they will have you call an 'officer' or install an app to 'update' the bill.

army-officer.name: Army-officer marketplace scam
army-officer.summary: A fake soldier on OLX or Quikr offers to pay in advance and sends a QR or request that actually takes your money.
army-officer.nextStep: Next they will send a QR code or collect request and ask you to scan or approve it.

loan-advance-fee.name: Advance-fee loan scam
loan-advance-fee.summary: An instant loan with no documents is 'approved', but you must pay a processing or GST fee before it is released.
loan-advance-fee.nextStep: Next they will demand a processing, insurance, or GST fee before any money arrives.

job-task.name: Job / task scam
job-task.summary: An easy work-from-home job promises daily earnings but asks for a registration fee or prepaid tasks first.
job-task.nextStep: Next they will ask you to recharge a 'task wallet' or pay a joining fee.

lottery-prize.name: Lottery / prize scam
lottery-prize.summary: You have 'won' a lottery you never entered; to claim it you must pay a fee and share personal details.
lottery-prize.nextStep: Next they will ask for a processing fee and your bank or Aadhaar details.

sim-swap.name: SIM / verification scam
sim-swap.summary: Your SIM will be 'deactivated' unless you re-verify — really an attempt to take over your number and OTPs.
sim-swap.nextStep: Next they will ask you to share the OTP or code sent to your phone.

card-upgrade.name: Card upgrade / reward-points scam
card-upgrade.summary: A free card upgrade or expiring reward points lure you into sharing your card number, CVV and OTP.
card-upgrade.nextStep: Next they will ask for your card number, CVV, and the OTP to 'activate' it.

investment-trading.name: Investment / trading scam
investment-trading.summary: A tips group promises guaranteed or doubled returns to lure a deposit into a fake trading app.
investment-trading.nextStep: Next they will ask you to deposit money into their app or wallet to start.

qr-receive.name: QR-to-receive scam
qr-receive.summary: You are told to scan a QR code to receive money — but scanning and entering a PIN pays money out.
qr-receive.nextStep: Next they will send a QR code and ask you to scan it and enter your UPI PIN.

phishing-link.name: Phishing link
phishing-link.summary: A message urges you to click a link to verify, reactivate or secure your account on a fake page.
phishing-link.nextStep: Next the fake page will ask for your login, card details, or OTP.

other.name: Suspicious message
other.summary: This message shows scam-like pressure but does not match a specific known pattern.
other.nextStep: Be cautious and verify independently before acting.

playbook.title: What to do now
playbook.intro: Follow these steps in order. Tap each one when it is done.

steps.dontClick: Do not click the link. Banks never ask you to update KYC through an SMS link.
steps.doNotShare: Do not share any OTP, PIN, CVV or password — no bank or official ever needs them.
steps.doNotPay: Do not pay, transfer, or approve any request right now.
steps.doNotInstall: Do not install any app they ask for (AnyDesk, TeamViewer, or similar).
steps.hangUp: Hang up or stop replying. A real official never rushes you or forbids you from telling family.
steps.breatheVerify: Pause and breathe. Pressure to act instantly is the scam — real institutions give you time.
steps.pinInvariant: Remember: entering your UPI PIN only sends money OUT. You never need a PIN, approval or QR scan to receive money.
steps.refundTruth: Never return money to a stranger. If a wrong amount really came in, your bank reverses it — you never handle it yourself.
steps.digitalArrestTruth: The police, CBI or courts never arrest you over a video call or ask for money to clear a case. This is always a scam.
steps.loanTruth: A genuine lender never asks for a fee before giving a loan. Any processing fee to release the amount is a scam.
steps.lotteryTruth: You cannot win a lottery you never entered, and no real prize needs a fee to release it.
steps.callBankOfficial: Call your bank on the number printed on your card or passbook — never a number from the message.
steps.freezeCard: Block or freeze your card and UPI in your official bank app.
steps.changePin: Change your UPI PIN and net-banking password.
steps.checkStatement: Check your account statement for any transaction you did not make.
steps.call1930: Call 1930, the National Cyber Crime Helpline, immediately — the first hour matters most.
steps.goldenHour: Report within the golden hour. Fast reporting can freeze the transfer and get your money back.
steps.fileComplaint: File a complaint at cybercrime.gov.in using the draft below.
steps.informBank: Tell your bank in writing to flag the fraudulent transaction.

complaint.heading: Ready-to-send complaint
complaint.intro: Fill in what you know, then copy the complaint and send it at cybercrime.gov.in or your police station.
complaint.template:
To the Cyber Crime Cell,

I wish to report a financial fraud of the type "{archetype}". On {date}, I received a fraudulent message attempting to cheat me.

Amount involved: Rs {amount}
Suspicious UPI ID / account / number: {vpa}

The message I received was:
"{message}"

Please register my complaint and take necessary action. I am also reporting this on the 1930 helpline.

Regards

link.title: Check a link
link.intro: Paste a suspicious link, or the whole message, to check it for phishing.
link.tips: Real banks use their own website and never ask you to log in through an SMS link. Watch for misspelled names, extra words, and odd endings like .xyz or .top.

upi.title: Check a UPI request
upi.intro: Answer two questions to know whether a UPI request is safe.
upi.q1: What kind of request is it?
upi.collect: A request asking me to pay or approve
upi.pay: I am sending money to someone
upi.q2: Did someone tell you this request is to RECEIVE money?
upi.invariant: Entering your UPI PIN always takes money OUT of your account. You never need a PIN, an approval, or a QR scan to receive money.
upi.resultScam: This is a scam. A collect request takes money FROM you when you approve it. Nobody who is sending you money needs you to approve or enter a PIN.
upi.resultCollectCaution: Careful: approving this request and entering your PIN will send money OUT. Only approve if you meant to pay someone you trust.
upi.resultPay: A pay request sends money out of your account. Approve only if you meant to pay this person.
upi.explainerPay: Pay: you send money out. It needs your PIN.
upi.explainerCollect: Collect: someone asks you to pay them. Approving it also sends money out — never to receive.

learn.title: Scam or Safe?
learn.intro: Practise spotting scams. You get 10 messages — decide if each is a scam or safe. Suraksha gives you more of the kinds you find tricky.
learn.whyScamGeneric: It uses pressure, a reward or a request for secret information to trick you.
learn.whySafeGeneric: This is a normal message. It does not ask for a PIN, OTP, payment or an app install.
learn.shareText: I scored {score} on Suraksha's scam-awareness drills. Learn to spot scams too — stay safe!

otp.title: What is an OTP?
otp.body: An OTP is a one-time password sent to your phone to approve something YOU started. No bank, company or officer ever needs your OTP. Anyone who asks for it is trying to steal from you.

receiveNoPin.title: Receiving money never needs a PIN
receiveNoPin.body: Your UPI PIN only ever sends money OUT of your account. To receive money you do nothing — no PIN, no approval, no QR scan. If someone says 'enter your PIN to get money', it is a scam.

checkLender.title: How to check if a lender is real
checkLender.body: A real lender never asks for a fee before giving a loan. Check the lender on the RBI website's list of registered NBFCs. 'No documents', 'guaranteed approval' and 'RBI approved' in a message are warning signs.

call.title: Call guard
call.honestyNote: The browser can't listen in on a phone call. Put the caller on speaker (or play a recording) so Suraksha can hear it, and watch the meter as they talk.
call.unsupported: Live listening needs Chrome or Edge. On this browser, paste what the caller said or texted into Check instead.
call.uploadTitle: Have a recording of the call?
call.uploadHint: Upload an audio file. It is transcribed on your device and checked — nothing is sent to any server.
call.transcribingHint: Reading the audio on your device…
call.downloadingModel: Downloading the transcription model once ({percent}%) — after this it works offline.

errors.unsupported: This browser can't transcribe audio here. Paste what was said into Check instead.
errors.decode: Couldn't read that audio file. Try a WAV or MP3 recording, or paste what was said into Check.
errors.model: Couldn't load the transcription model. Connect to the internet for the first use, then try again.
errors.empty: No clear speech was found in that recording. Try again somewhere quieter, or paste what was said into Check.

call.transcriptEmpty: The call will appear here as it is spoken…
call.dangerWarning: This is a scam call. Do not share any OTP or PIN, do not pay, and do not install anything. No real bank or officer works like this.

pwa.installPitch: Install Suraksha on your phone — it opens like an app and works offline.
